items.title: Amazon OpenSearch Serverless now supports a 5-second default refresh interval
items.content_snippet: Starting today, Amazon OpenSearch Serverless reduces the default refresh interval to 5 seconds for both search and vector collections. The refresh interval controls how quickly newly ingested documents become available for search. By lowering the default from 10 seconds to 5 seconds, newly written data becomes searchable faster, giving applications quicker read-after-write visibility automatically, with no configuration changes and no action required on your part. items.title: AWS CloudFormation now simplifies stack update rollback operations
items.content_snippet: AWS CloudFormation now makes it simpler to complete an update rollback and get back to deploying. An update rollback returns your stack to a known good state. Starting today, if some resources cannot roll back automatically, force rollback enables you to complete the rollback it in a single operation. items.title: Uber rolls out ChatGPT Work to 30,000+ employees
items.content_snippet: Following a 1,000-person pilot, Uber is bringing ChatGPT Work to more than 30,000 employees worldwide in its first company-wide deployment of an agentic platform for knowledge work. Uber CTO Praveen Neppalli Naga and OpenAI co-founder and President Greg Brockman discuss expanding AI beyond engineering and helping teams rethink entire workflows. items.title: A Bank Trained Its Own Foundation Model to Catch Fraud — Freddy Lecue, Wells Fargo
items.content_snippet: Freddy Lecue explains how Wells Fargo pre-trained its own transformer from scratch on billions of customer transactions instead of words. The model learns to predict the next transaction, and that one backbone can then be fine-tuned for fraud detection, credit line decisions, anti-money laundering and marketing. items.title: How to Let AI Agents Sign Up for Your App Safely — Isabelle Williams, WorkOS
items.content_snippet: Isabelle Williams, a product manager at WorkOS, uses a travel app she built to show how to make an app ready for users who arrive as agents. She covers auth.md, an open file that tells agents how to get access; an anonymous mode where an agent can try the app before a person claims its work; and ID-JAG identity assertions, which let the agent's provider vouch for the user so nobody has to fill in a signup form. items.title: Don't Trust Your AI Agents. Test Them Like a Scientist — Stephanie Jarmak, Omni Analytics
items.content_snippet: Stephanie Jarmak, a former astronomer who now builds evals at Omni Analytics after building a large coding benchmark at Sourcegraph, argues that most agent evaluations are easy to misread. items.title: Why AI Startups Will Disappear Without Compute Markets — Evan Conrad, San Francisco Compute
